stem:
Rosa, Sam, Tess, Uly and Vic sit in a row of five chairs, numbered 1 to 5 from left to right.
- Tess sits in chair 3.
- Rosa sits at one end of the row.
- Sam sits next to Rosa.
- Uly does not sit next to Tess.

Which must be true?
hints: Rosa can be at either end, so there are two cases. Work out both.
Case 1: Rosa in chair 1. Case 2: Rosa in chair 5. In each case, place Sam next to Rosa, and remember Tess is in chair 3.
In each case, two chairs are left for Uly and Vic. Uly cannot be in chair 2 or 4, because those are next to Tess. Finish both rows. The answer is the choice that is true in both.

solution.methodName: Line them up, then test every case

steps.action: Tess is in chair 3. Rosa is at an end, so she is in chair 1 or chair 5. Try both cases.
steps.why: When a clue allows two options, work out each one. A choice must be true in every case to be the answer.

steps.action: Case 1: Rosa in chair 1. Sam must be next to her, in chair 2. Chairs 4 and 5 are left. Chair 4 is next to Tess, so Uly takes chair 5 and Vic takes chair 4. Row: Rosa, Sam, Tess, Vic, Uly.
Case 2: Rosa in chair 5. Sam must be in chair 4. Chairs 1 and 2 are left. Chair 2 is next to Tess, so Uly takes chair 1 and Vic takes chair 2. Row: Uly, Vic, Tess, Sam, Rosa.
"Vic sits next to Tess": Vic is in chair 4 in case 1 and in chair 2 in case 2. Both are next to chair 3. It is true in both cases, so it must be true.
steps.why: Vic always gets the chair beside Tess, because Uly is not allowed there.

steps.action: "Rosa sits in chair 1" and "Uly sits in chair 5" are true in case 1 but false in case 2. They could be true, but they do not have to be.
"Uly sits next to Sam" is false in both cases: in case 1 Uly is in chair 5 and Sam in chair 2; in case 2 Uly is in chair 1 and Sam in chair 4.
The answer is "Vic sits next to Tess."

This is true only in case 1. Counterexample (case 2): Uly, Vic, Tess, Sam, Rosa. Every clue holds, and Rosa is in chair 5.
This is true only in case 1. Counterexample (case 2): Uly, Vic, Tess, Sam, Rosa. Every clue holds, and Uly is in chair 1.
This is false in both cases. In case 1 Uly is in chair 5 and Sam in chair 2; in case 2 Uly is in chair 1 and Sam in chair 4. They are never side by side.
